# Original Kerotakis text, CC BY 4.0; model-assisted editorial draft, 2026-09-07.
# Preserved law/control lessons; no new imported constants or output tables.

[[reaction]]
id = "three-components-one-cut"
progress = "advanced"
summary = "A computed distillation cut moves three components without creating or discarding any of them"
concepts = ["phase-change", "latent-heat", "conservation-of-mass", "model-boundary"]
requires = ["amount-of-substance", "mixtures"]
calculations = ["enthalpy-change"]
models = ["massenerhaltung", "chemisches-gleichgewicht", "enthalpie"]
apparatus = ["distillation-flask", "condenser", "beaker"]

[reaction.setup]
script = """
add v1 water 3mol
add v1 methanol 0.3mol
add v1 isopropanol 0.2mol
new
distil v1 v2 0.2
inspect v1
inspect v2
"""

[reaction.expect]
events = ["distilled"]
absent = ["solver_failed"]

[reaction.expect.predict]
question = "Does the most volatile component arrive alone in the receiver?"
options = ["Yes: distillation transfers one component at a time", "No: the vapor is a mixture, and every component must be counted in both vessels"]
answer = 1
misconception = "Enrichment is confused with perfect separation; a mixed vapor can favor one component without excluding the others."

[[reaction.expect.predict.diagnosis]]
option = 0
reveals = "A boiling-point ordering is mistaken for a sequence of pure-component withdrawals."
next = "Add each component's remaining and collected amounts, then compare the receiver composition with the starting composition."

[reaction.registers]
lv1 = "The receiver gets a mixture, not just the easiest component to evaporate; what moved out of the source must appear somewhere else."
lv2 = "The starting total is 3 + 0.3 + 0.2 = 3.5 mol, so a molar cut fraction of 0.2 requests 0.7 mol in total, not that fraction of every component; check each component separately across the source and receiver."
lv3 = "The generic Rayleigh calculation uses ideal Raoult mixing and a bounded constant-latent Clausius–Clapeyron approximation; it does not predict nonideal azeotropes or measured apparatus performance, and reported duty sums withdrawn condensate latent heat only, excluding sensible heating and reflux/reboiler circulation."

[reaction.provenance]
source = "Original audit-derived lesson; conservation and cut-fraction arithmetic, existing reviewed USCG CHRIS still inputs and existing water latent reference; no new imported data. Editorial judgement (Kerotakis), model-assisted draft, 2026-09-07."
computed_by = "Kerotakis generic multicomponent Rayleigh solver; independent third/fourth-fleet component and latent-duty checks"

[[reaction]]
id = "equal-charge-different-clocks"
progress = "intermediate"
summary = "Equal delivered charge gives equal modeled water-electrolysis production despite different current schedules"
concepts = ["electrolysis", "faraday-law", "charge-conservation"]
requires = ["amount-of-substance"]
calculations = ["faraday"]
models = ["stoechiometrie", "massenerhaltung"]
apparatus = ["beaker", "power-supply"]

[reaction.setup]
script = """
add v1 water 250mL
add v1 KNO3 0.001mol
electrolyse v1 0.2A 60s
new
add v2 water 250mL
add v2 KNO3 0.001mol
electrolyse v2 0.1A 120s
new
add v3 water 250mL
add v3 KNO3 0.001mol
electrolyse v3 0.2A 30s
electrolyse v3 0.2A 30s
inspect v1
inspect v2
inspect v3
"""

[reaction.expect]
events = ["electrolysed:H2", "gas_evolved:H2", "gas_evolved:O2"]
absent = ["solver_failed"]

[reaction.expect.predict]
question = "Which current schedule produces the most hydrogen in this water-electrolysis model?"
options = ["The largest current always produces the most", "All three schedules produce the same amount because they deliver equal charge"]
answer = 1
misconception = "Current is treated as an amount instead of a rate of charge delivery; the duration and the sum over separate pulses are missing."

[[reaction.expect.predict.diagnosis]]
option = 0
reveals = "An instantaneous setting is used to predict a total without integrating over time."
next = "Multiply current by duration for each pulse and add the pulses, then compare the generated electrode-product amounts rather than only the gas remaining in the open vessels."

[reaction.registers]
lv1 = "A smaller current can catch up by running longer, and splitting a delivery does not erase its first part."
lv2 = "Each schedule delivers Q = It = 12 C; with water in excess the model gives n(H2) = Q/(2F) and n(O2) = Q/(4F), so compare cumulative electrode production rather than treating escaped gas as missing production."
lv3 = "These controls test the existing ideal charge-to-product model, not measured current efficiency, electrode overpotential or apparatus gas collection; the independent atom ledger balances final contents against external gas evolved minus absorbed, counting retained headspace gas only in contents and never adding production events as another material reservoir."

[reaction.provenance]
source = "Original audit-derived control lesson; Faraday charge/stoichiometry arithmetic using the existing runtime Faraday constant, no new imported data. Editorial judgement (Kerotakis), model-assisted draft, 2026-09-07."
computed_by = "Kerotakis generic solvent-electrolysis operator and ordinary aqueous/gas stack; independent third-fleet charge and external-flow atom checks"

[[reaction]]
id = "grouping-does-not-change-water-heat"
progress = "intermediate"
summary = "Grouping the same three water portions differently preserves their final sensible-energy balance"
concepts = ["calorimetry", "heat-capacity", "state-functions"]
requires = ["amount-of-substance"]
calculations = ["enthalpy-change", "temperature-rise"]
models = ["enthalpie", "massenerhaltung"]
apparatus = ["beaker", "thermometer"]

[reaction.setup]
script = """
new
add v2 water 1mol
heat v2 300J
new
add v3 water 2mol
cool v3 200J
new
add v4 water 3mol
heat v4 100J
new
mix v2 1 v3 1 into v5
mix v5 1 v4 1 into v1
measure v1 thermometer
new
add v6 water 1mol
heat v6 300J
new
add v7 water 2mol
cool v7 200J
new
add v8 water 3mol
heat v8 100J
new
mix v7 1 v8 1 into v9
new
mix v6 1 v9 1 into v10
measure v10 thermometer
"""

[reaction.expect]
events = ["mixed", "temperature_changed", "measured"]
absent = ["solver_failed"]
# From 25 + (300 - 200 + 100)/(6 * 75.3), not a stored simulation answer.
temperature_c = { min = 25.44, max = 25.45 }

[reaction.expect.predict]
question = "Does combining the warmer pair first change the final temperature when all three water portions are eventually combined?"
options = ["Yes: the first mixture sets a temperature that the later mixture remembers", "No: the same total water and retained sensible energy determine the final temperature"]
answer = 1
misconception = "Intermediate temperature is treated as conserved, rather than the energy carried by each amount of water."

[[reaction.expect.predict.diagnosis]]
option = 0
reveals = "Unweighted intermediate temperatures replace an amount-weighted energy balance."
next = "Sum the energy additions and removals, divide by the total heat capacity, and compare the final thermometers in v1 and v10."

[reaction.registers]
lv1 = "Different intermediate temperatures can lead to the same final temperature when the same water and energy end up together."
lv2 = "Each branch starts with 6 mol of water at 25 °C and retains 300 - 200 + 100 = 200 J; with the existing water heat capacity of 75.3 J/(mol K), the final temperature follows from 25 + 200/(6 × 75.3), regardless of grouping."
lv3 = "This is an adiabatic, constant-heat-capacity sensible-energy control for water with no phase transition or reactive mixing; it does not claim that real vessels lose no heat, or that grouping preserves temperature if material escapes or different chemistry occurs along the paths."

[reaction.provenance]
source = "Original audit-derived control lesson; sensible-energy conservation with the existing water heat-capacity input, no new imported data. Editorial judgement (Kerotakis), model-assisted draft, 2026-09-07."
computed_by = "Kerotakis generic heating/cooling and material-conserving MIX; independent third-fleet three-water energy/associativity checks"
